sections.markdown:
## C2 — Parking, transporting and maritime confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A143
Near a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights, moving over and slowing to at least 10 mph under the limit are alternatives, and you must do one of them. [A143]
Why it matters: group_hint emergency-zone; prereq_hint sec11-F01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F02.
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A143
In an emergency zone, slowing to 10 mph under the posted limit is a minimum drop, and 50 mph is an absolute ceiling no matter how high the posted limit is. [A143]
Why it matters: group_hint emergency-zone; prereq_hint sec11-R01; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F02, sec11-F03.
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A143
The 30-foot gap applies to traffic signals, stop signs and yield signs, the 5-foot gap to driveways, alleys and private roads, and the 75-foot gap to a fire station driveway across the street. [A143]
Why it matters: group_hint parking-distances; prereq_hint sec11-F05; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F07, sec11-F08, sec11-F09.
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A144
Fire hydrants need a 15-foot gap, pedestrian safety zones a 20-foot gap and railroad crossings a 50-foot gap, while the tracks themselves allow no parking at all. [A144]
Why it matters: group_hint parking-distances; prereq_hint sec11-R03; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F10, sec11-F11, sec11-F12.
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A144
The 12-inch limit is a maximum distance from the curb, and white curbs allow brief stops while yellow or red curbs mean loading or other limits. [A144]
Why it matters: group_hint curb-rules; prereq_hint sec11-F06; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F13, sec11-F15.
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A145
The under-16 rule covers a child left in a parked vehicle with the engine running, while the under-12 rule covers a child left alone in any parked vehicle. [A145]
Why it matters: group_hint unattended; prereq_hint sec11-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F18, sec11-F19.
Source: [A145 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0145]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A148
Uphill against a tall curb you turn the wheel away so the tire's back edge catches the curb, but with a low or rounded uphill curb turning toward it may be safer. [A148]
Why it matters: group_hint hill-parking; prereq_hint sec11-F16; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F27, sec11-F28.
Source: [A148 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A149
Downhill the wheel turns toward the curb so the front of the tire meets it, and with no curb the wheels turn toward the road edge, away from traffic. [A149]
Why it matters: group_hint hill-parking; prereq_hint sec11-R07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F29, sec11-F30.
Source: [A149 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A147
Entering a parallel space starts by backing until bumpers line up with the car you park behind, and it ends no more than 12 inches from the curb. [A147]
Why it matters: group_hint parking-maneuvers; prereq_hint sec11-F24; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F24, sec11-F25.
Source: [A147 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A151
An animal in a truck bed is legal only with a protective harness or enclosure, while transporting any animal in a risky way is a separate misdemeanor offense. [A151]
Why it matters: group_hint animals; prereq_hint sec11-F36; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F36, sec11-F37.
Source: [A151 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A152
Beach driving is limited to two counties with a 25 mph limit, and walkers and cyclists keep the right-of-way there at all times. [A152]
Why it matters: group_hint maritime; prereq_hint sec11-F41; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F41, sec11-F42.
Source: [A152 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0152]
